subject: physics
question_text: When a bullet is fired from a gun, the gun gives a kick in the backward direction. Explain.

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), Unit 5 VERY SHORT ANSWER. The 1+1 mark split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed for this question, so appearances[] stays empty.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The law used
lines: Before firing, the gun and the bullet
are at rest, so the total momentum is
zero. No external force acts, so
steps.margin_note: Name the law in words — "conservation of linear momentum" is what the examiner looks for.
steps.why: The explosion pushes gun and bullet apart, but that force is internal to the pair. Internal forces can never change the total momentum.
common_mistakes: Saying only "reaction" without naming a law.

recall.must_convey: That the total momentum before firing is zero and momentum is conserved.
accept: total momentum before firing is zero

steps.memory_tip: Start at rest: total momentum 0 before firing, so 0 after.

steps.label: Why it kicks back
lines: The bullet gains forward momentum, so
the gun must gain an equal momentum

steps.margin_note: Say "equal momentum", not "equal velocity" — the gun is far heavier, so it moves much slower.
steps.why: Equal and opposite MOMENTA, not equal speeds. The heavy gun carries the same momentum at a small speed, which is why the kick is survivable.
common_mistakes: Writing that the gun moves back with the same SPEED as the bullet.

recall.must_convey: That the forward momentum of the bullet is matched by an equal backward momentum of the gun.
accept: bullet forward gun backward equal momentum

steps.memory_tip: The bullet goes forward, so the gun must go backward with EQUAL momentum — not equal speed.
